contexts.story: Open by framing the talk around one core question: how should engineers evolve their careers as AI rapidly changes the nature of our work, roles, and the skills that matter most?
Introduce Chao’s career evolution not as the main story, but as a lens that illustrates how AI work has shifted from traditional computer vision to LLM-based systems and product-integrated AI.
Show how the nature of AI work has changed—from linear, accuracy-obsessed projects to cyclical, orchestration-focused systems—so the audience can see why old career playbooks no longer fit.

Highlight where the highest-return technical work now lies—reliability, evaluation, and feedback loops—so engineers can redirect effort from chasing tiny accuracy gains to building systems that actually succeed in the real world.

Explain how human–AI co-creation and cross-domain thinking change what it means to ‘solve a problem,’ pushing engineers to design iterative experiences and combine tools rather than just ship one-off models.

Use a concrete LLM system pattern to show how modern AI work blends reasoning, tooling, and state management, giving the audience a mental model for how to think about building robust AI-powered features.
Distill the evolving landscape into three high-ROI focus areas that engineers can deliberately invest in to stay valuable and impactful in the LLM era.
Show how treating AI tools as leverage and single sources of truth—rather than threats—can multiply an engineer’s impact and free time for higher-level thinking.
Emphasize the mindset shift required for a durable AI career: repeatedly becoming a beginner, tracking where the field is going, and aligning your growth with those shifts.
Close with a simple operating principle—making every step of your work solid—as a practical way to turn daily tasks into compounding expertise in a fast-moving AI world.
